job.title: Construction Manager
job.description:
Construction Manager
We’re working with a successful, family-owned contractor that has grown quickly and is now strengthening its leadership structure. They’re looking for a Construction Manager to take ownership of delivery across the Lower north island.

This is a practical, visible leadership role. You’ll work across the projects, build strong relationships with an experienced group of Project Managers and help them deliver consistently. The business has good people and a solid pipeline of work. It now needs a senior construction leader who can give the team the support and direction to match its growth.

What you’ll do
  • Take overall responsibility for construction delivery across a varied portfolio of commercial projects.
  • Stay close to the work through regular site visits, project meetings and conversations with clients and PMs.
  • Help PMs work through programme, buildability, quality and client issues before they become bigger problems.
  • Set clear expectations and follow up on performance, while giving experienced people the space to do their jobs.
  • Improve visibility across projects so leadership has a clear picture of progress, risks and issues.
  • Work closely with the Commercial Manager and QS team to understand project performance and take responsibility for delivery outcomes.
What you’ll bring
You’ll have a strong commercial construction background and experience delivering larger projects, with $20m-plus projects a useful guide. You’ll know what good looks like on site and be confident discussing methodology, programme, quality and buildability with experienced PMs.

You’ll also bring the people judgement this role needs. The team is established and capable, and each person has had a high degree of autonomy. You’ll need to earn their trust, offer practical support and be comfortable setting clear expectations when needed.

Strong commercial awareness matters, particularly when it comes to understanding project performance and asking the right questions. You won’t need to be the person preparing every cost report, but you will need to understand what the numbers are telling you and work well with the commercial and QS teams.

Why consider it
The business is growing and putting clearer leadership around its construction operation. You’ll work directly with the GM and alongside an incoming Commercial Manager, with a strong QS team around you.

There’s a genuine opportunity to shape how delivery works across the business.

Leadership values autonomy and backs people to get on with the job, with clear expectations and support when it’s needed.

If you’d like to understand the role in more detail, contact Ginny at RWR Construction for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Site Manager
job.description:
We’re partnering with an established New Zealand construction business to find an experienced Site Manager for confirmed projects across Northland.

With a long history across commercial and public-sector construction, the business is also growing its capability in offsite and modular delivery, combining factory-built elements with full onsite construction.

You’ll be dedicated to your project and trusted to run the site with minimal day-to-day input from the Project Manager. You’ll make the calls, solve problems as they arise and keep the project moving - bringing your PM solutions and recommendations rather than a list of decisions to make.

You’ll own the site from establishment and enabling works through to installation, onsite completion and final handover. Programme, subcontractors, quality, H&S, materials, site records and the day-to-day performance of the project all sit within your remit. That can include classroom buildings, civil and enabling works, services, ablution facilities, accessibility infrastructure and substantial associated site works. Current projects include multi-level modular construction, so we're looking for someone who understands the whole build, not simply the installation of a prefabricated building.

Experience delivering education or other public-sector projects would be valuable. Modular, offsite or prefab experience would also be an advantage, but neither is essential if you've got strong commercial site-management foundations.

You’ll run the programme, coordinate subcontractors, manage inspections and deliveries, maintain quality and H&S standards and make sure the site is ready for each stage of the build.

There’s a commercial element to the position too. You'll understand subcontractor scopes, budgets, dayworks and variations, and make sure additional work is properly identified and recorded before value disappears.
You'll also take ownership of materials. The QS may place the orders, but you'll make sure the right materials are actually onsite when they're needed - including the seemingly small items capable of bringing a trade to a halt.

And your involvement won't necessarily begin on day one onsite. The goal is to increasingly involve Site Managers during pre-construction, contributing practical delivery knowledge to programmes, P&Gs, resource requirements and subcontractor scopes before the job starts. 

You could already be a strong Site Manager with a commercial main contractor, running projects with very little input from your PM.

You might be a Senior Foreman ready to take the next step, provided you can demonstrate that you've genuinely owned programme, subcontractors and delivery rather than simply supervised trades.

Or you could be a Junior/Assistant Project Manager who has strong construction knowledge and prefers being close to the action onsite.
Whatever your title, you'll know how a building goes together. You'll be confident reading drawings and specifications, understand the NZ construction and inspection environment and be capable of running a project through to a clean, low-defect handover.

Just as importantly, you'll know how to lead people. You'll be able to hold subcontractors accountable without unnecessarily damaging relationships and represent the business professionally with clients, consultants, school staff and the wider public.

You'll need to be comfortable with technology This business is actively moving away from paper-heavy site management.

Procore is used to run the site, and diaries, H&S, QA, photos, RFIs, drawings, defects and variations are expected to be kept current as the work happens - not uploaded retrospectively because the PM has chased for them.
Experience with Procore or a similar platform would be ideal. More important is being digitally capable, quick to learn and interested in using technology - including emerging AI tools - to work smarter. 

There's genuine ownership here. You'll be trusted to run your site rather than having a Project Manager looking over your shoulder. The expectation is high, but you'll have the autonomy to match it.

You'll also be delivering projects with a tangible community impact, particularly across the education sector, while gaining exposure to a business investing in a growing offsite and modular construction capability.

If you're the Site Manager who likes being handed the job and trusted to own the outcome, we'd like to hear from you.

For a confidential conversation, reach out to Max at maximilianc@rwrconstruction.co.nz.

job.title: Site Manager
job.description:
This is a strong opportunity for a developing Site Manager who already has a solid grounding in commercial construction and is ready to step into more responsibility.

The Auckland team is currently busy delivering modular Ministry of Education projects, with classrooms being built off-site and then installed across live school environments. The current workload is heavily focused on education, but the wider direction is expected to broaden further into private and commercial projects as the Auckland operation continues to grow.

They are looking for someone who is still relatively early in their Site Management career but has enough commercial experience behind them to understand how a site should run.

Ideally, you will have around 4+ years’ commercial construction experience, with exposure across areas such as light commercial, retail, dealerships, education, industrial or similar project environments. Broader build experience is preferred over someone who has only worked in fit-out, although strong fit-out candidates with transferable site delivery experience could still be considered.

An LBP would be highly regarded, particularly given the practical nature of the role.

Day to day, you will be involved across subcontractor coordination, short-term planning, programme delivery, QA, H&S, materials, site meetings and communication with the wider project team. You will need to be comfortable keeping trades moving, identifying issues early and making sure the next stage of work is properly lined up.

Because of the modular environment, the role also requires someone who can work across both factory and live-site delivery. There are tight deadlines, multiple moving parts and a need for clear communication between the factory, site teams and wider project management team.

There will also be a FIFO travel component, with work across two locations in the Waikato and Gisborne. Travel costs will be covered by the business, so you will need to be comfortable being away from Auckland when projects require it.

This is not an overly corporate Site Management role. They want someone practical, proactive and comfortable getting close to the work. You should be the type of person who can step in, solve problems and keep things moving rather than waiting for someone else to make the call.

The role could suit a strong Foreman, Site Supervisor, Assistant Site Manager or developing Site Manager who is looking for a genuine next step and wants to continue building their commercial experience.

You do not need to be the finished article. What is more important is that you have a good commercial foundation, can communicate well, understand programme and site coordination, and have the attitude to keep developing.
There is good support around the role, but equally, they are looking for someone who wants ownership and is motivated to grow with the Auckland operation as the project mix expands.

If you have solid commercial site experience, enjoy being close to delivery and are comfortable with some FIFO travel, this is well worth a conversation.

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
If you're a Project Manager who likes having ownership of your projects rather than needing five layers of approval to get something done, this could be worth a conversation.

We're working with a privately owned commercial construction business that's adding to its delivery team off the back of a strong forward workload.
They deliver predominantly Design & Build projects across commercial, industrial, retail and warehouse environments, with several projects currently moving through design and into construction across the North Island.

This is a newly created role rather than a replacement.

About the role.
 
Reporting to the Construction Director, you'll take responsibility for your own projects and work closely with clients, consultants, subcontractors and the wider delivery team.

With a strong Design & Build focus, you won't simply be handed a completed set of drawings and told to build it.

You'll be involved across the wider project, coordinating consultants, working through design and buildability issues, managing programme and subcontractors, and ultimately taking ownership of getting the job delivered.

The business has systems and processes in place, but they're not looking for someone who needs a huge corporate structure around them. Their PMs are given room to run their projects, make decisions and adapt when things change.

There will be some travel depending on the projects you're delivering, with work currently spread across the upper North Island and occasionally further afield.

About you.

My client is interested in someone who understands construction, can take ownership and knows how to work with clients, consultants and subcontractors to get a project delivered.

An LBP and/or qualified carpentry background would be a significant advantage.
 
The business places real value on PMs who have practical construction knowledge behind them and understand how things actually get built.

Ideally, you'll bring:
  • Commercial construction experience at Project Manager level
  • LBP and/or qualified carpentry background - highly regarded
  • Design & Build experience, ideally including consultant coordination
  • Strong programming and subcontractor management capability
  • Confidence dealing directly with clients and consultants
  • A practical understanding of construction and buildability
  • Good systems and technology capability
  • The ability to take ownership of your projects without working in a silo
  • A collaborative, solutions-focused approach when things don't go to plan
They're not looking for someone overly rigid or set in their ways. The environment changes quickly, so being adaptable, willing to muck in and comfortable finding a way forward is important.
 

If you've come through the tools, hold your LBP, have progressed into running commercial sites and are already taking on broader responsibility across programme, subcontractors, clients or consultants, don't rule yourself out because your current title says Site Manager.

You don't necessarily need to be the finished article.

For the right person, this could be an opportunity to bring the practical construction experience you've already developed and broaden that into responsibility for the wider project.

Why consider it?
 
This is a growing business with a good pipeline of work and a delivery model that gives its people genuine responsibility.

You'll get exposure to Design & Build rather than sitting purely at the construction end of a project, and you'll work closely with the people making decisions within the business.

It's a relatively straightforward environment: good systems where they're needed, autonomy where it makes sense, and an expectation that you'll take responsibility for what you're delivering.

For an established PM, there's the opportunity to have more ownership.
For someone stepping up from Site Management, there's the opportunity to develop the broader project management side without losing the value of your practical background.

Package
 
Remuneration is flexible and will depend on the experience and capability you bring.

The wider package includes a company vehicle and project-performance incentives.

If you're an established commercial Project Manager looking for more ownership, or an LBP/Site Manager wondering whether you're ready to take that next step, I'd be keen to hear from you.

Apply now or contact Maximilian Collins at RWR Construction for a confidential conversation. maximilianc@rwrconstruction.co.nz

job.title: Site Engineer
job.description:
Get closer to the construction and build your career. We’re working with a growing New Zealand civil contractor delivering technically challenging infrastructure projects across Three Waters, pipelines, treatment facilities, structures, piling and specialist civil works.

They self-perform much of their work, with their own crews, plant and engineering capability. For a Site Engineer, that means genuine exposure to how projects are built, rather than simply managing subcontractors.

** Please note, this position is based in the Hawkes Bay & requires relocation**

The role:

Working alongside experienced Project Managers, Engineers and Supervisors,

you’ll take responsibility for packages of work and get involved across:
  • Planning and sequencing site activities
  • QA, ITPs and project documentation
  • Construction methodology and temporary works
  • Programme, productivity and cost monitoring
  • Procurement and subcontractor coordination
  • Working directly with site crews
  • Identifying and solving construction issues
  • Supporting commercial and project reporting
You’ll bring:
  • Strong technical fundamentals
  • A genuine interest in construction methodology
  • Initiative and the ability to think ahead
  • Good communication with both site crews and professional teams
  • A willingness to learn and take feedback
  • Ownership of your work
  • A practical, down-to-earth approach
What we’re looking for Ideally, you’ll have a Civil Engineering degree and some practical construction experience.

Experience across water, wastewater, drainage, pipelines, structures, piling or heavy civil infrastructure would be useful, but attitude and technical ability are just as important.

You’ll enjoy being on site, getting into the detail and understanding how things are actually built. You’ll be proactive, comfortable taking responsibility and keen to keep developing.

Why consider it?

You’ll get exposure to complex projects, experienced technical leaders and considerably more construction responsibility than you might within a heavily subcontracted environment.

If you’re an ambitious Civil Engineer looking to accelerate your development and work on interesting infrastructure projects, get in touch for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Senior Estimator
job.description:
The Opportunity:

We're partnering with an established New Zealand civil contractor looking for an experienced Civil Estimator to join its Auckland team.

This is a lean, commercially focused business delivering civil infrastructure projects across New Zealand, with work spanning earthworks, drainage, utilities, retaining structures, rail and general civil construction.

The contractor works alongside major Tier 1 organisations while also delivering its own projects as head contractor, predominantly using its own crews, with project values extending up to the $10M–$40M range.

They're looking for an estimator who can do more than price work — they want someone who understands how to win the right projects and deliver profitable outcomes.

The Role You'll be responsible for:
  • Pricing civil infrastructure projects across multiple disciplines.
  • Building detailed rates and estimates using Candy.
  • Reviewing drawings, specifications and tender documentation.
  • Identifying commercial, contractual and project risks.
  • Taking genuine ownership of tenders from start to finish.
  • Working closely with commercial, engineering and delivery teams.
  • Understanding project performance beyond tender award.
  • Helping the business secure profitable work.
What We're Looking For:
  • 5–10+ years' civil estimating experience.
  • Strong knowledge of the New Zealand civil construction market.
  • Broad experience across earthworks, drainage, utilities, retaining structures, rail and/or general civil works.
  • Strong commercial judgement alongside technical estimating capability.
  • Confidence interpreting drawings, specifications and contractual requirements.
  • Experience following projects from tender through delivery, claims and close-out.
  • A track record of understanding and protecting project margins.
  • Candy experience or strong experience with comparable estimating systems.
A Tier 1 civil contracting background would be highly regarded, particularly if you're looking to move away from a larger corporate structure and take greater ownership of your work.

Why Consider It?

 This is an opportunity to join a smaller, agile contractor where your contribution will be visible and your commercial judgement will matter.

You'll find:
  • Greater ownership and accountability.
  • Less corporate bureaucracy.
  • Broad exposure across civil disciplines.
  • A direct and commercially focused environment.
  • The opportunity to influence which projects the business pursues and wins.
  • Remuneration that can reflect the capability and value you bring.
They're not looking to simply fill a vacancy. The priority is finding an estimator with the right combination of technical capability, commercial thinking and attitude.

If you tick the above boxes and are keen to find out more, apply today or reach out to Alex on 027 370 7011 or alexb@rwrconstruction.co.nz

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
An established and growing New Zealand infrastructure contractor is looking for an experienced Project Manager to join its Auckland operation.
The business delivers a range of specialist infrastructure projects across Auckland and the wider region, working with major public and private sector clients.

This is an opportunity to take genuine ownership of projects from award through to completion. You'll work closely with clients, field teams, subcontractors and suppliers, with responsibility for ensuring projects are delivered safely, commercially and to programme.

This is a hands-on Project Management position where you'll remain close to both the client and what's happening on site.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Managing infrastructure projects from planning through to completion and handover
  • Developing programmes and coordinating labour, subcontractors, materials and equipment
  • Managing project budgets, costs, claims and variations
  • Maintaining visibility over project margins and commercial performance
  • Building strong relationships with clients and key stakeholders
  • Coordinating internal delivery and field teams
  • Managing subcontractors and suppliers
  • Identifying project risks and resolving delivery issues early
  • Ensuring projects are delivered safely, efficiently and to the required quality
  • Providing accurate project reporting across programme and financial performance
  • Supporting repeat business through strong project delivery and client relationships
We're looking for someone who understands how to take ownership of a project rather than simply administer it.

You'll ideally bring:
  • Proven Project Management experience within infrastructure, civil construction, utilities or a similar contracting environment
  • Experience managing projects from award through to handover
  • Strong commercial understanding and confidence managing project costs
  • Experience coordinating field teams, subcontractors and suppliers
  • Strong client and stakeholder management skills
  • The ability to manage multiple priorities and keep projects moving
  • A practical approach to problem solving and decision making
  • Good communication skills across both site and senior client stakeholders
  • A strong understanding of health, safety and quality in a contracting environment
We're open to different infrastructure backgrounds. More important is someone who understands contracting, is commercially switched on and can confidently take responsibility for their projects.

What's On Offer You'll be joining a well-established New Zealand contractor with a strong pipeline of infrastructure work and continued growth ahead.
The business has a practical, down-to-earth culture and gives its Project Managers the autonomy to take responsibility for their projects rather than operating within unnecessary layers of management.

For someone who enjoys being across the commercial, operational and client sides of delivery, this is an opportunity to take genuine ownership and play an important part in the continued growth of the Auckland operation.

If you tick the above boxes & would like to find out more, apply today or reach out to Alex on 027 370 7011 or alexb@rwrconstruction.co.nz

job.title: Construction Manager
job.description:
This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who wants genuine ownership of a civil operation.

You’ll be leading an established team of around 25 across a mix of water, wastewater, stormwater, utilities and wider civil infrastructure projects. There’s a solid base already in place, but there’s also plenty of opportunity to bring the teams closer together, strengthen how things operate and help shape where the business goes next.

You’ll have the freedom to make decisions, improve things that aren’t working and develop the people around you. For someone who likes the idea of running an operation rather than simply managing a portfolio of projects, there’s a lot to get your teeth into.

The role
Reporting into the senior leadership team, you’ll take responsibility for the performance of the construction operation across multiple projects and teams.

That will include:
  • Leading Project Managers, Supervisors and site teams across multiple civil projects
  • Keeping a close eye on programme, resources, productivity and project performance
  • Owning budgets, forecasting, cost control and commercial outcomes
  • Making sure contracts are being managed properly and risks are picked up early
  • Building strong relationships with clients, consultants and other stakeholders
  • Developing the people underneath you and creating clear accountability across the team
  • Looking at systems, processes and ways of working and improving them where needed
  • Supporting tendering, client relationships and opportunities to grow the operation
  • Maintaining strong safety, quality and environmental standards
Who are we looking for?
You could already be operating as a Construction Manager, or you may be a strong Senior Project Manager, Contracts Manager or operational leader who is ready to take on a broader business.

You’ll need a solid civil construction background and experience leading multiple projects and people. Three Waters experience would be particularly useful, although we’re open to broader civil infrastructure backgrounds where the fundamentals are strong.

You’ll understand the commercial side of construction as well as delivery. Contracts, margins, forecasting, programming and resource planning shouldn’t be things that sit solely with someone else.

The person behind the experience matters too.

We’re looking for someone who takes ownership, works hard and has good judgement. You’ll be comfortable making decisions independently, but equally comfortable asking questions, listening to your team and bringing people with you when things need to change.

You don’t need to arrive with all the answers. You do need to be curious enough to work out what could be better and have the drive to do something about it.

Why consider it?
The attraction here is the amount of influence you can have. This is a smaller operation where you’ll be close to the people doing the work and close to the people making the decisions. Good ideas can actually be acted on.

There are established clients, an experienced team and a broad portfolio of civil work already in place, but there is also genuine scope to improve the operation and help build what comes next.

If you’ve spent time in a larger contractor and like the idea of having more ownership, or you’re already running teams and want a role with broader operational responsibility, it’s worth a conversation.

You don’t need to be actively looking. If this has caught your attention, get in touch with Ginny Ryder at RWR Construction for a confidential chat.

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
About the Company:

We're working with one of New Zealand's leading specialists in water treatment and process infrastructure. They deliver complex design and build projects across municipal and industrial sectors, combining in-house engineering, fabrication, construction and commissioning under one roof.

With around 100 staff, this business has built an outstanding reputation delivering complex water infrastructure projects nationwide.
The culture is collaborative, practical and hands on. People are trusted to make decisions, take ownership and contribute to the continued growth of the business.

Internal development is genuinely encouraged, with many senior leaders having progressed through the organisation.

As demand continues to grow, they're looking for a Project Manager who can take ownership of multidisciplinary projects from early design coordination through to successful delivery on site.

You'll be involved from the earliest stages of a project, coordinating consultants, working alongside process and mechanical engineers, managing civil and building interfaces, and ensuring projects are delivered safely, commercially and to programme.

Projects typically range from around $500k through to well into the multi million dollar range and are located throughout New Zealand.

You'll be responsible for:
  • Managing projects from design through to construction and commissioning
  • Coordinating civil, structural, mechanical, electrical and process disciplines
  • Managing external consultants and subcontractors
  • Working closely with internal engineering and fabrication teams
  • Overseeing programme, commercial performance and client relationships
  • Travelling to project sites throughout New Zealand as required, typically around one week per month
About You:

We're open on background, but you'll ideally bring experience delivering multidisciplinary infrastructure or industrial projects.

You might come from:
  • Three Waters
  • Water or wastewater treatment
  • Industrial or process plants
  • Mechanical services
  • Civil infrastructure
  • Heavy industrial construction
More importantly, you'll have:
  • Proven experience managing projects from design through to completion
  • Strong understanding of coordinating multiple disciplines
  • Confidence managing subcontractors and consultants
  • Excellent communication and client management skills
  • Commercial awareness and programme management capability
  • The ability to work autonomously and take ownership
What's on Offer:
  • Salary circa $150,000-$170,000 depending on experience
  • Work on technically interesting, multidisciplinary projects
  • National project exposure across New Zealand
  • Genuine autonomy and ownership
  • Strong pipeline of secured work
  • Long-term career development within a growing organisation
  • Supportive, high-performing team culture
If you're looking for a Project Management role where you'll be involved in far more than simply delivering construction, we'd love to have a confidential chat.

Apply now or contact Alex on 027 370 7011 or alexb@rwrconstruction.co.nz
